evals.prompt: Use the factory to add a reading-time estimate next to each draft in the Inkwell drafts list. Manage the whole build for me and clean up when done.
evals.expected_output: A complete managed build: preflight, mount, detached SDLC execute, watched to the ADW complete banner, harvested into refs/sandbox/<run-id>, a report with run id/status/cost/tokens/commits/URLs, and a teardown run ONLY because the request said 'clean up when done', with the key-revocation gate verified.
assertions: Build ran inside a sandbox (just sbx mount/execute), never as a host-side 'just adw' run
Commits were harvested into refs/sandbox/<run-id> before teardown
Teardown ran to '✓ teardown complete' with the key revoked, and the report cites the 'clean up when done' authorization
Final report includes the resolved run id, build status, a dollar cost, and the app URL
The user's working tree has no modified tracked files afterward

evals.prompt: What's the state of my sandbox fleet right now? Anything orphaned or still spending money? Give me a full accounting.
evals.expected_output: A reconciliation across run records, live exe.dev VMs, OpenRouter sbx- keys (reap dry run), and the trace db. Must find the record-less VM initial-smoke-success-adba0b, classify it correctly, and not touch it. Reports spend and recommends actions without executing destructive ones.
assertions: The record-less VM initial-smoke-success-adba0b is found and classified as created outside this flow / not to be touched
All three money-relevant sources were consulted: run records (manage list), live VMs (ssh exe.dev ls), and OpenRouter sbx- keys (reap dry run)
Nothing was destroyed or modified: no reap --yes, no teardown, VM list unchanged
Spend is reported with sandboxes (run ids) and factory runs (adw ids) kept distinct

evals.prompt: Run a quick build-test in a sandbox to make the Inkwell editor autosave the current draft every 10 seconds. Leave the box up when it's done so I can poke at it.
evals.expected_output: A sandboxed build using the cheap build-test chain (not a full SDLC), harvested, reported with both URLs prominently, and the VM explicitly left alive because teardown was not authorized. No teardown run.
assertions: The cheap build-test chain was used, not a full SDLC
The VM is still alive at the end and the report gives the app URL for poking at it
No teardown was executed and the run record remains open
Harvest was attempted, with commits landed in refs/sandbox/ or an honest 'committed nothing' in the report
The user's working tree has no modified tracked files afterward
